newsitem.title: THAILAND: Khashoggi's shares in Thai firm frozen.
newsitem.headline: Khashoggi's shares in Thai firm frozen.

text.p: Thai police said on Wednesday they had frozen shares worth 142 million baht ($5.5 million) held by Saudi tycoon Adnan Khashoggi in a local firm Jalaprathan Cement Plc.
An arrest warrant was issued last week by Thai police for Khashoggi, 61, wanted here on charges of conspiring to defraud ailing local bank, the Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc.

"I have received a report from the economic crime investigation police that they have ordered the freezing of the shares of Adnan Khashoggi worth 142 million baht in Jalaprathan Cement Plc," Thai police chief, Pracha Promnok, told reporters.
The freezing of the tycoon's shares were part of an exercise to recover part of the bank's losses, he said.

Police said they were also looking into allegations that Bangkok Bank of Commerce executives had helped Khashoggi take out loans from the bank, with a substantial portion of them used for his investment in Thai stocks, including in cement-maker Jalaprathan.

The arrest warrant for Khashoggi and four other officials of the troubled bank was issued at the request of the Thai central bank on suspicion that they jointly conspired for Khashoggi to draw two billion baht in loans from Bangkok Bank of Commerce in 1995 without credible collateral.

The whereabouts of the globe-trotting Saudi businessman, once one of the world's richest men, are unknown. But his multi-million dollar deals, court cases and elite acquaintances have spread his fame throughout the world.
Among those sought by Thai police along with Khashoggi were the bank's former president, Krirkkiat Jalichandra, and former advisor Rakesh Saxena.
Police last week arrested a Briton, Terry Easter, who was suspected of violating the Thai Banking Act, resulting in 1.66 billion baht in losses for the bank.

Bangkok Bank of Commerce, saddled with non-performing loans totalling more than 70 billion baht, was taken over by the government last year after opposition charges of the debts trigggered a run on its deposits.
Earlier on Wednesday, trading in shares of Jalaprathan were suspended by the Thai bourse pending more details from the firm on a proposed capital increase.
Jalaprathan officials declined to comment on the police statement when contacted by Reuters.
After the arrest warrant was issued last week, Khashoggi said in published remarks on Sunday that he was preparing a response to the Thai charges and was hopeful of an amicable settlement.
He denied in an article quoting him in the Saudi daily al-Eqtisadiah that he knew any of the others accused with him in the Bangkok Bank of Commerce case.
